The card lists those neighbors and the result, degree 4." width="100%"} For directed graphs, returns total degree (in-degree + out-degree). For undirected graphs, returns the number of neighbors. More precisely, the degree is the number of edges touching the node: parallel edges each count, and in undirected graphs a self-loop counts twice. Edge weights are ignored. Use this for a quick check on a single node, for example while exploring a graph or inside a `conditions=` or `select_nodes()` callback. To get every node's degree at once, use `degrees()`; for one direction only in a directed graph, use `get_in_degree()` or `get_out_degree()`. The graph is not modified. In directed graphs the in-degree part is counted by scanning the whole edge list, so each call takes time proportional to the number of edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to query, given either as its integer node ID or as its string label (e.g., `3` or `"A"`). A string is always treated as a label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degree of the node. An isolated node has degree `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `node=` is an ID or label that does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `A` is connected to both `B` and `C`, so its degree is `2`. Nodes can be referred to by label: ::: {#a7b6398b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C")]) ) graph.get_degree("A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: `B` only touches the edge to `A`, so its degree is `1`. Here it is looked up by its node ID instead: ::: {#f6b3cc06 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_degree(graph.get_id_from_label("B")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: In directed graphs, degree counts both directions combined -- here "A" has one outgoing and one incoming edge, for a total degree of `2`: ::: {#a0dc813c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), # out for A, in for B ("C", "A"), # in for A ] ) ) graph.get_degree("A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
